intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with variation in several genes. These include HLA-DRB1 (142857) on chromosome 6p21.32, PTPN22 (600716) on chromosome 1p13.2, SLC22A4 (604190) on chromosome 5q31.1, RUNX1 (151385) on chromosome 21q22.12, STAT4 (600558) on chromosome 2q32.2-q32.3, TRAF1 (601711) on chromosome 9q33.2, CD244 (605554) on chromosome 1q23.3, AFF3 (601464) on chromosome 2q11.2, CTLA4 (123890) on chromosome 2q33.2, BLK (191305) on chromosome 8p23.1, CCR6 (601835) on chromosome 6q27 and FCGR3B (610665) on chromosome 1q23.3. A variant of CD44 (107269) on chromosome 11p13 has been found in RA synovial fluid cells, and a polymorphism in IL10 (124092) on chromosome 1q32.1 has been associated with disease progression.

paragraphs.text: Rheumatoid arthritis is the most common systemic autoimmune disease. It affects about 1% of adults worldwide and has an estimated heritability of 60% (Begovich et al., 2004). Tamiya et al. (2005) described RA as a destructive joint disease that affects up to 1% of the population. Barton et al. (2001) described RA as an oligogenic autoimmune disease. They noted that the only consistent genetic finding had been linkage and association to the MHC, which is estimated to account for only 30 to 40% of the total genetic component of susceptibility.

paragraphs.text: Ito et al. Two of 23 patients with psoriatic arthritis (8.7%) were positive. None of 11 patients with osteoarthritis, 30 with systemic lupus erythematosus or 10 with polymyositis/dermatomyositis were positive. Ito et al. (2014) tested synovial fluid from 24 RA patients and 9 healthy individuals and found CD4+ T cells that produced IFN-gamma on stimulation with recombinant RPL23A in a subset of the RA patients. RPL23A mRNA was expressed ubiquitously in healthy human tissues. RPL23A protein was present in the cytoplasm of synovial cells, including CD55+ fibroblast-like synoviocytes, in both RA and osteoarthritis synovium. The authors suggested that these responses may have a pathogenic role in at least a subset of patients with RA or psoriatic arthritis.

The analyses included first-degree relatives from 135 simplex and 30 multiplex families. The most parsimonious genetic risk factor was a highly penetrant recessive major gene with a mutant allele frequency of 0.005. The authors suggested that families with an excess of affected males with young age at onset may be the most informative for identifying this putative recessive gene and its modifiers.

paragraphs.text: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) estimated that the variants they newly identified together explained only 0.6% of the variance in RA risk, and that all known non-MHC common variants explained 3.6%. About 60% of RA risk is thought to be genetic, with one-third of that from the MHC, so the authors concluded that known risk alleles explain less than half of the genetic variation. Stahl et al. (2010) estimated that the more than 30 validated non-MHC RA risk alleles explain 3.9% of total disease variance, of which 0.67% is due to the new alleles they reported. Known genetic factors overall, including an estimated 12% for the MHC, explained only 16% of disease variance. In contrast, more than half the risk of autoantibody-positive RA is thought to be genetic.

paragraphs.text: Cornélis et al. (1998) carried out a genome scan in 114 European Caucasian RA sib pairs from 97 nuclear families. Linkage was significant only for HLA (P less than 2.5 x 10(-5)). Linkage was nominal (P less than 0.05) for 19 markers in 14 other regions, 4 of which possibly overlap with loci implicated in IDDM (IDDM6, IDDM9, IDDM13 and DXS998). They then examined the 18q22-q23 candidate region (D18S68-D18S61-D18S469) and the 3q13 candidate region (D3S1267) in a further 194 RA sib pairs from 164 nuclear families. Only the chromosome 3 region showed significantly extended support for linkage (P = 0.002). Across all 261 families the evidence for linkage was P = 0.001. The authors suggested that this putative RA locus interacts with HLA and could account for 16% of the genetic component of RA. They proposed the genes encoding CD80 and CD86 as candidates.

paragraphs.text: Cox et al. (1999) studied the interleukin-1 (IL-1) gene cluster on chromosome 2q13 in RA families using the combined sib-TDT and TDT together with parametric and nonparametric linkage methods. Several tightly linked IL-1 cluster markers gave suggestive evidence for linkage in the combined TDT in families in which affected sibs did not share 2 HLA-DRB1 alleles identical by descent. The evidence was significant in patients with severe, erosive disease. Nonparametric linkage analysis showed no evidence of linkage, and parametric analysis gave weak evidence only when marker-trait disequilibrium was included. The authors considered the data preliminary evidence for linkage of IL-1 cluster genes to RA.

paragraphs.text: Jawaheer et al. paragraphs.text: Jawaheer et al. (2002) performed haplotype analysis with 54 markers across the HLA complex in 469 multicase RA families. paragraphs.text: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) performed a genome-wide association study of about 2,000 British Caucasian patients with RA, who met the 1987 American College of Rheumatology criteria, and 3,000 shared controls. They confirmed strong association with the MHC/HLA-DRB1 region on 6p21; the strongest MHC SNP was rs6457617 (trend P = 3.44 x 10(-76)). Rheumatoid arthritis was the only one of the 7 diseases studied in which a sex-differentiated analysis produced a strong signal. SNP rs11761231 on 7q32 gave P = 3.9 x 10(-7) on the 2-df sex-differentiated test. It had no effect in males (P = 0.68) but an additive effect in females (P = 6.8 x 10(-8); OR 1.32), although the authors advised caution in interpreting this result. Moderate evidence of association (P between 10(-5) and 5 x 10(-7)) was found at 9 SNPs, none at previously reported RA loci. These SNPs included rs2104286 near IL2RA, rs743777 near IL2RB and rs6920220 on 6q23 (trend P = 4.99 x 10(-6)). When RA and type 1 diabetes cases were combined, the IL2RA/CD25 region on 10p15 reached P = 5 x 10(-8). Weaker signals were seen in TNFAIP2, GZMB, PRKCQ and KAZALD1. Two CTLA4 SNPs were only nominally significant (P = 0.085 and 0.034).

paragraphs.text: Thomson et al. (2007) genotyped 9 SNPs that had been putatively associated with RA in the WTCCC screen in an independent UK cohort of 5,063 RA cases and 3,849 controls. Only rs6920220 (G>A) replicated (OR for the minor allele = 1.23; trend P = 1.1 x 10(-8)). The combined trend P value with the WTCCC data was 3.6 x 10(-12) (OR = 1.22). This SNP lies in a 60-kb linkage disequilibrium block on 6q23 that contains no known genes but includes part of a PTPN11 pseudogene. The block lies between OLIG3 and TNFAIP3; the authors noted that TNFAIP3 negatively regulates NF-kappa-B and that TNFAIP3-deficient mice develop multiorgan inflammation, including joint inflammation. rs6920220 did not interact with the HLA-DRB1 or PTPN22 susceptibility markers. Together, the HLA-DRB1 shared epitope, PTPN22 rs2476601 and rs6920220 accounted for 8.5% of the total variance in RA susceptibility. The PTPN22 rs2476601 association was confirmed in this cohort (OR = 1.53; trend P = 2.0 x 10(-18)). There was modest evidence of association for IL2RB rs743777 (combined trend P = 5.3 x 10(-6)) and borderline evidence for the sex-differentiated effect of rs11761231 near PODXL (trend P = 0.042). IL2RA rs2104286 was not associated with RA.

paragraphs.text: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) carried out a meta-analysis of 2 genome-wide association studies of RA comprising 3,393 cases and 12,462 controls of European ancestry. They then genotyped 31 top-ranked SNPs not previously associated with RA in 3,929 autoantibody-positive cases and 5,807 controls; 6 of the SNPs reached P of 0.01 or less. They identified association with rs4810485 in intron 2 of CD40 on 20q13 (overall P = 8.2 x 10(-9); OR 0.87 for the minor T allele). This SNP is in near-perfect linkage disequilibrium with rs1883832, a variant associated with autoimmune thyroid disease that affects CD40 translation efficiency. They also identified association with rs2812378 near the 5-prime UTR of CCL21 on 9p13 (overall P = 2.8 x 10(-7); joint OR 1.12). Evidence of association was found at 4 further loci, which required further validation: MMEL1-TNFRSF14 (1p36), CDK6 (7q21), PRKCQ (10p15) and KIF5A-PIP4K2C (12q13). The meta-analysis also showed association at PTPN22, 6q23 (TNFAIP3), STAT4, TRAF1-C5, 4q27 (IL2/IL21) and CTLA4, but not at PADI4.

paragraphs.text: Orozco et al. (2009) fine-mapped the 6q23 locus by genotyping 70 SNPs in 3,962 UK RA patients of Northern European descent and 3,531 controls; 18 SNPs were associated with RA. The strongest association was with rs6920220 (P = 2.61 x 10(-7), OR 1.22), which tagged a risk haplotype. The next strongest was rs13207033 (P = 0.0001, OR 0.86), which was perfectly correlated with rs10499194 and whose minor allele was protective. The authors described this as the first independent replication of the rs10499194 association. They also identified a new potential marker, rs5029937, in intron 2 of TNFAIP3. Conditional regression suggested 3 independent effects. The functional exon 3 TNFAIP3 polymorphism rs2230926, which had been associated with SLE, was not independently associated with RA.

The scan confirmed associations with the MHC (maximum P = 9.50 x 10(-104)), PTPN22 rs2476601 (P = 1.62 x 10(-21)) and the TRAF1/C5 region (rs881375, P = 4.09 x 10(-8)).

paragraphs.text: Stahl et al. (2010) performed a GWAS meta-analysis of 5,539 autoantibody-positive RA cases and 20,169 controls of European descent and replicated the results in 6,768 cases and 8,806 controls. Ten SNPs reached genome-wide significance, 7 of them at new RA risk loci, bringing the number of confirmed risk loci in individuals of European ancestry to 31. Three of the loci had not been implicated in any autoimmune disease: rs934734 in SPRED2 (2p14), rs6859219 in ANKRD55 (5q11), about 150 kb from IL6ST, and rs26232 in C5orf30 (5q21). Three loci had previously been implicated in other autoimmune diseases: rs13315591 near PXK (3p14), rs874040 near RBPJ (4p15) and rs3093023 in CCR6 (6q27). The IRF5 SNP rs10488631 was associated with autoantibody-positive RA (P overall = 4.2 x 10(-11)), with an independent effect of rs4728142. At CCL21, a new SNP, rs951005, had effects partly independent of rs2812378. At IL2RA, rs706778 was associated with RA, but the type 1 diabetes risk haplotype rs2104286(T)-rs11594656(T) explained RA risk better. The authors provided definitive evidence for association of AFF3 (rs11676922; P overall = 1.0 x 10(-14); OR = 1.14). Eleven more SNPs, near genes including IL6R, CD247, IL2/IL21, SH2B3 and UBE2L3, replicated at P less than 0.05 without reaching genome-wide significance.

paragraphs.text: Plenge et al. (2007) performed a genomewide association study of 317,503 SNPs in 1,522 anti-CCP-positive RA cases and 1,850 matched controls from the NARAC and Swedish EIRA collections. They replicated top SNPs in 997 cases and 1,777 controls. In all samples, association was seen with the MHC, with PTPN22 and with rs3761847 on chromosome 9 (OR 1.32; 95% CI 1.23-1.42; P = 4 x 10(-14)). rs3761847 is in linkage disequilibrium with TRAF1 and C5. The authors concluded that a common variant at the TRAF1-C5 locus increases the risk of anti-CCP-positive RA.

paragraphs.text: Remmers et al. (2007) tested SNPs in and around 13 candidate genes in the previously linked chromosome 2q region. A SNP haplotype in the third intron of STAT4, marked by rs7574865, was associated with RA. paragraphs.text: Barton et al. (2009) genotyped 18 SNPs at 14 previously suggested type 1 diabetes loci in 3,962 UK RA cases and 3,531 controls. They identified association with rs10865035 at the AFF3 locus on chromosome 2. In a combined analysis of 6,819 cases and 12,650 controls, the OR was 1.12 (P = 2.8 x 10(-7)). The associated variants map to the 5-prime and promoter region of AFF3, which is preferentially expressed in lymphoid cells. paragraphs.text: Yen et al. (2001) studied Caucasians of Western European descent: 76 controls, 70 RA patients without major organ involvement and 30 patients with rheumatoid vasculitis. The authors concluded that KIR2DS2 did not affect the risk of developing RA but was strongly associated with vascular complications. Compared with controls, RA patients had a decreased frequency of HLA-C*04 (OR 0.39) and an increased frequency of HLA-C*05 (OR 2.92). checks.evidence_quote: After entering both genes into the model, each demonstrated an independent significant risk associated with vasculitis (odds ratio for HLA-C*03 = 8.6, P < 0.001; odds ratio for KIR2DS2 = 3.69, P = 0.01), suggesting that both contribute a risk to vasculitis, independent of each other.
checks.explanation: The logistic regression model showed independent risk for each gene.

paragraphs.text: Remmers et al. (2007) reported that homozygosity for the STAT4 risk allele, compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a 60% increased risk for RA and a more than doubled risk for SLE.

checks.claim: Homozygosity for the STAT4 risk allele, compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a 60% increased risk for RA.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity of the risk allele, as compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a more than doubled risk for lupus and a 60% increased risk for rheumatoid arthritis.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the 60% increased risk for RA.

checks.claim: Homozygosity for the STAT4 risk allele, compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a more than doubled risk for SLE.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity of the risk allele, as compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a more than doubled risk for lupus
checks.explanation: The abstract states the more than doubled risk for SLE.

paragraphs.text: Thomson et al. (2007) found that the rs6920220 association was stronger in anti-CCP-positive and rheumatoid factor-positive patients. In the WTCCC data, the OR was 1.38 in anti-CCP-positive patients and 1.03 in anti-CCP-negative patients, and the difference was significant in the combined cohorts (trend P = 0.003). The authors suggested that RA may comprise at least 2 genetically distinct subsets.

checks.claim: The rs6920220 association with RA was stronger in anti-CCP-positive patients.
checks.evidence_quote: stronger associations were again observed in the antibody-positive subjects (Table 2)
checks.explanation: The association was stronger in anti-CCP-positive subjects in both the WTCCC data and the combined cohorts.

checks.claim: The rs6920220 association with RA was stronger in rheumatoid factor-positive patients.
checks.evidence_quote: The same pattern was seen in rheumatoid factor-positive and negative subgroups (Table 2).
checks.explanation: Table 2 shows stronger association in rheumatoid factor-positive subjects (combined OR 1.28 vs 1.08).

checks.claim: In the WTCCC data, the rs6920220 OR was 1.38 in anti-CCP-positive RA patients and 1.03 in anti-CCP-negative RA patients.
checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of the WTCCC study indicated a significant association for SNP rs6920220 in anti-CCP-positive (OR = 1.38, 95% CI = 1.22-1.55, trend P = 1.7 × 10-7) but not in anti-CCP-negative individuals (OR = 1.03, 95% CI = 0.82-1.29).
checks.explanation: Both odds ratios match the paper.

checks.claim: The difference in rs6920220 association between anti-CCP-positive and anti-CCP-negative RA was significant in the combined cohorts (trend P = 0.003).
checks.evidence_quote: Indeed, the difference between the anti-CCP-positive and negative subgroups was statistically significant (trend P = 0.003).
checks.explanation: The surrounding text places this result in the combined WTCCC and validation cohorts.

checks.claim: Thomson et al. (2007) suggested that RA may comprise at least 2 genetically distinct subsets.
checks.evidence_quote: the clinical phenotype of rheumatoid arthritis may actually comprise at least two genetically distinct subsets, one of which is characterized by the presence of antibody to CCP
checks.explanation: The paper makes this suggestion directly.

paragraphs.text: Barton et al. (2009) found similar strengths of association at the AFF3, CTLA4 and IL2/IL21 SNPs in autoantibody-positive and autoantibody-negative patients.

checks.claim: Barton et al. (2009) found similar strengths of association at the AFF3, CTLA4 and IL2/IL21 SNPs in autoantibody-positive and autoantibody-negative RA patients.
checks.evidence_quote: following stratification by presence of auto-antibodies, the strength of associations was similar between auto-antibody positive and negative individuals at all three SNPs indicated by the overlapping confidence intervals
checks.explanation: The three SNPs are at AFF3, CTLA4 and IL2/IL21.

paragraphs.text: Orozco et al. (2009) found that rs6920220 and rs5029937 at 6q23 appeared to be associated with autoantibody-positive RA. In contrast, rs13207033 was associated with both RF-positive and RF-negative cases but only with anti-CCP-negative cases. All 3 SNPs were associated in both sexes. Carrying the risk alleles of rs6920220 and rs5029937 together with absence of the protective allele of rs13207033 was strongly associated with RA compared with carrying none of them (OR 1.86). This high-risk combination was carried by 4.4% of patients and 2.3% of controls.

checks.claim: SNPs rs6920220 and rs5029937 at 6q23 appeared to be associated with autoantibody-positive RA.
checks.evidence_quote: rs6920220 and the intron 2 SNP, rs5029937, appeared to be associated with auto-antibody positive cases, with strong association in both RF positive and anti-CCP positive cases.

checks.claim: SNP rs13207033 at 6q23 was associated with both RF-positive and RF-negative RA.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast, rs13207033 was associated with both RF positive and negative RA cases, but only anti-CCP negative cases.

checks.claim: SNP rs13207033 at 6q23 was associated only with anti-CCP-negative RA cases.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast, rs13207033 was associated with both RF positive and negative RA cases, but only anti-CCP negative cases.

checks.claim: SNPs rs6920220, rs5029937 and rs13207033 at 6q23 were each associated with RA in both sexes.
checks.evidence_quote: Stratification analysis of the three independently associated RA SNPs showed that all three SNPs were associated with both male and female RA cases

checks.claim: Carrying the risk alleles of rs6920220 and rs5029937 together with absence of the protective allele of rs13207033 was strongly associated with RA compared with carrying none of them (OR 1.86).
checks.evidence_quote: The combination of the carriage of both risk alleles of rs6920220 and rs5029937 together with the absence of the protective allele of rs13207033 was strongly associated with RA when compared with carriage of none [OR of 1.86 (95% CI) (1.51–2.29)].

checks.claim: The high-risk 6q23 combination (risk alleles of rs6920220 and rs5029937 plus absence of the protective rs13207033 allele) was carried by 4.4% of RA patients and 2.3% of controls.
checks.evidence_quote: (4.4% of the RA patients versus 2.3% of the controls carried this high-risk combination)
checks.explanation: The percentages match. They come from data pooled with the earlier WTCCC GWAS cohort.

paragraphs.text: Gregersen et al. (1987) proposed the shared epitope hypothesis as an approach to understanding the molecular genetics of susceptibility to RA. Weyand et al. (1992) suggested that the disease-associated sequence motif in the third hypervariable region of HLA-DRB1 has a role in determining RA severity. They also suggested that HLA-DR function in thymic selection might be important in RA pathogenesis.

checks.claim: Gregersen et al. (1987) proposed the shared epitope hypothesis as an approach to understanding the molecular genetics of susceptibility to RA.
checks.evidence_quote: The shared epitope hypothesis. An approach to understanding the molecular genetics of susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied, but it states the claim directly: the paper presents the shared epitope hypothesis as an approach to understanding the molecular genetics of susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis.

checks.claim: Weyand et al. (1992) suggested that the disease-associated sequence motif in the third hypervariable region of HLA-DRB1 has a role in determining RA severity.
checks.evidence_quote: Our data suggest a role of the disease-associated sequence motif in determining severity of the disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract places this motif in the third hypervariable region of HLA-DRB1 in its first sentence.

checks.claim: Weyand et al. (1992) suggested that HLA-DR function in thymic selection might be important in RA pathogenesis.
checks.evidence_quote: the biological function of HLA-DR molecules in thymic selection might be important in the pathogenesis of RA.

paragraphs.text: Nanki et al. (1996) studied T cell receptor BJ gene expression in peripheral T lymphocytes from 12 pairs of monozygotic twins, including 6 pairs discordant for RA, and from 5 normal individuals. BJ repertoires were more similar in monozygotic twins than in unrelated individuals, and RA inflammation did not induce specific changes in the pattern. The authors concluded that expression of particular TCRBV-TCRBJ recombinants is genetically controlled.

checks.claim: Nanki et al. (1996) studied T cell receptor BJ gene expression in peripheral T lymphocytes from 12 pairs of monozygotic twins and 5 normal individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: compared peripheral T lymphocytes from 12 pairs of monozygotic twins, including 6 rheumatoid arthritis (RA) discordant pairs, and 5 normals
checks.explanation: The abstract states 12 monozygotic twin pairs plus 5 normals. It does not say whether "5 normals" means individuals or pairs, so the draft's "5 normal individuals" is one reasonable reading.

checks.claim: Of the 12 monozygotic twin pairs studied by Nanki et al. (1996), 6 pairs were discordant for RA.
checks.evidence_quote: 12 pairs of monozygotic twins, including 6 rheumatoid arthritis (RA) discordant pairs

checks.claim: T cell receptor BJ repertoires were more similar in monozygotic twins than in unrelated individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: (c) the BJ gene repertoires of monozygotic twins are more similar than those of unrelated individuals

checks.claim: RA inflammation did not induce specific changes in the T cell receptor BJ repertoire pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: (d) the inflammation of RA does not induce specific changes in the genetically determined pattern of BJ expression

checks.claim: Nanki et al. (1996) concluded that expression of particular TCRBV-TCRBJ recombinants is genetically controlled.
checks.evidence_quote: These results indicate that the frequency of expression particular TCRBV-TCRBJ recombinants in human lymphocytes is controlled genetically
checks.explanation: The draft restates the authors' conclusion, which the abstract gives in these words.

paragraphs.text: Müller-Ladner et al. (2000) found IL-4 STAT mRNA in synovium from patients with both short-term and long-term RA. Expression was most intense in follicular inflammatory infiltrates and was present in both fibroblasts and macrophages of the synovial lining. IL-4 STAT was phosphorylated, which showed that it was activated. The authors concluded that IL-4 STAT-dependent pathways operate in early and late RA.

checks.claim: IL-4 STAT mRNA was found in synovium from patients with both short-term and long-term RA.
checks.evidence_quote: IL-4 STAT mRNA could be detected in synovium of patients with short-term and long-term RA.

checks.claim: IL-4 STAT expression in RA synovium was most intense in follicular inflammatory infiltrates.
checks.evidence_quote: The most intensive expression of IL-4 STAT mRNA could be seen in follicular inflammatory infiltrates.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly (the finding concerns mRNA expression).

checks.claim: IL-4 STAT was expressed in both fibroblasts and macrophages of the RA synovial lining.
checks.evidence_quote: In the synovial lining, both fibroblasts and macrophages expressed IL-4 STAT mRNA.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly (at the mRNA level).

checks.claim: IL-4 STAT in RA synovium was phosphorylated, showing that it was activated.
checks.evidence_quote: IL-4 STAT and Jak-1 protein was expressed by synoviocytes, and up-regulation could be induced after stimulation with IL-4. Activation of IL-4 STAT was reflected by phosphorylation of IL-4 STAT.
checks.explanation: The abstract says phosphorylation showed that IL-4 STAT was activated. It comes right after the IL-4 stimulation of synoviocytes, so the activation may have been shown in stimulated cells rather than in RA synovium itself. The abstract does not say which.

checks.claim: Müller-Ladner et al. (2000) concluded that IL-4 STAT-dependent pathways operate in early and late RA.
checks.evidence_quote: IL-4 STAT-dependent pathways operate in early and late stages of the disease
checks.explanation: This is the authors' stated conclusion.

paragraphs.text: Yen et al. (2001) found that 58 to 91% of CD4+CD28null T-cell clones from 3 patients with rheumatoid vasculitis expressed KIR2DS2, often unopposed by inhibitory receptors. Cross-linking enhanced IFN-gamma transcription and proliferation of these clones. The authors suggested that KIR2DS2 may contribute to vascular damage.

checks.claim: Yen et al. (2001) found that 58 to 91% of CD4+CD28null T-cell clones from 3 patients with rheumatoid vasculitis expressed KIR2DS2.
checks.evidence_quote: Of the activating receptors, expression of KIR2DS2 was prominent and ranged from 58–91% of the clones in the three patients studied.

checks.claim: KIR2DS2 on CD4+CD28null T-cell clones from rheumatoid vasculitis patients was often unopposed by inhibitory receptors.
checks.evidence_quote: These data demonstrate that in patients with rheumatoid vasculitis, KIR2DS2 was frequently unopposed by inhibitory receptors of related specificities on CD4+CD28null T cells.
checks.explanation: The paper says this directly. Its wording is more specific: the inhibitory receptors are those of related specificity (KIR2DL2/KIR2DL3).

checks.claim: Cross-linking of KIR2DS2 enhanced IFN-gamma transcription and proliferation of CD4+CD28null T-cell clones.
checks.evidence_quote: Enhancement of IFN-γ production by costimulation with GL183 was seen in five additional CD4+CD28null T cell clones that constitutively expressed KIR2DS2 or were transfected with KIR2DS2. Also, cross-linking with GL183 increased T cell proliferation in response to suboptimal anti-CD3
checks.explanation: Cross-linking was done with the anti-CD158b antibody GL183 on clones expressing KIR2DS2 but not KIR2DL2 or KIR2DL3. It raised IFN-gamma transcription and proliferation. The proliferation data were not shown and were cited to reference 33.

checks.claim: Yen et al. (2001) suggested that KIR2DS2 may contribute to vascular damage.
checks.evidence_quote: Specifically, KIR2DS2 in conjunction with the appropriate HLA-C ligand may have a role in vascular damage by regulating CD4(+)CD28(null) T cells.

paragraphs.text: Schaller et al. (2001) used phage display to clone highly somatically mutated, high-affinity human monoclonal anti-GPI IgGs from a patient with RA, indicating an affinity-matured, antigen-driven response. GPI was present at high concentrations on the synovial lining surface and on the endothelial surface of arterioles in RA synovium. The authors concluded that the immunologic events leading to arthritis in the K/BxN mouse model may also occur in human RA.

checks.claim: Schaller et al. (2001) used phage display to clone highly somatically mutated, high-affinity human monoclonal anti-GPI IgGs from a patient with RA.
checks.evidence_quote: Using phage-display methods, we cloned a panel of specific high-affinity human monoclonal anti-GPI IgGs from a patient with RA. These antibodies were highly somatically mutated
checks.explanation: The abstract matches the claim: phage display, high-affinity human monoclonal anti-GPI IgGs, one RA patient, and high somatic mutation.

checks.claim: The highly somatically mutated, high-affinity anti-GPI IgGs from an RA patient indicated an affinity-matured, antigen-driven response.
checks.evidence_quote: These antibodies were highly somatically mutated, which was indicative of an affinity-matured response that was antigen driven.
checks.explanation: The abstract draws the same conclusion: an affinity-matured, antigen-driven response.

checks.claim: GPI was present at high concentrations on the synovial lining surface in RA synovium.
checks.evidence_quote: Immunohistochemistry of RA synovium showed high concentrations of GPI on the surface of the synovial lining

checks.claim: GPI was present at high concentrations on the endothelial surface of arterioles in RA synovium.
checks.evidence_quote: showed high concentrations of GPI on the surface of the synovial lining and on the endothelial cell surface of arterioles

checks.claim: Schaller et al. (2001) concluded that the immunologic events leading to arthritis in the K/BxN mouse model may also occur in human RA.
checks.evidence_quote: The results indicate that the immunological events that lead to the development of autoimmune disease in the K/BxN mouse model may also occur in human RA.
checks.explanation: The abstract says "autoimmune disease" in the K/BxN model where the draft says "arthritis". The opening sentence calls that disease inflammatory arthritis, so the wording is equivalent.

paragraphs.text: Leadbetter et al. (2002) showed that effective activation of B cells expressing rheumatoid factor was mediated by IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes. Activation required synergistic engagement of the antigen receptor and a MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor, and inhibitor studies implicated TLR9.

checks.claim: Effective activation of B cells expressing rheumatoid factor was mediated by IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that effective activation of RF+ B cells is mediated by IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes

checks.claim: Activation of rheumatoid factor-expressing B cells required synergistic engagement of the antigen receptor and a MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: requires the synergistic engagement of the antigen receptor and a member of the MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor (TLR) family

checks.claim: Inhibitor studies implicated TLR9 in activation of rheumatoid factor-expressing B cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Inhibitor studies implicate TLR9.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly. In context, it refers to the activation of RF+ B cells.

paragraphs.text: Okamoto et al. (2003) suggested that the MHC may contain RA determinants that affect both innate immunity, through IkappaBL and NF-kappa-B, and adaptive immunity, through HLA-DRB1.

checks.claim: Okamoto et al. (2003) suggested that the MHC may contain RA determinants that affect innate immunity through IkappaBL and NF-kappa-B.
checks.evidence_quote: I kappa B alpha, the latter being a known inhibitor of NF kappa B, which is central to innate immunity. Therefore, the MHC may harbor RA genetic determinants affecting the innate and adaptive arms of the immune system.
checks.explanation: The abstract links IkappaBL and NF-kappa-B to innate immunity and concludes that the MHC may hold RA determinants affecting it.

checks.claim: Okamoto et al. (2003) suggested that the MHC may contain RA determinants that affect adaptive immunity through HLA-DRB1.
checks.evidence_quote: Therefore, the MHC may harbor RA genetic determinants affecting the innate and adaptive arms of the immune system.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions adaptive immunity, but it never says that HLA-DRB1 is the determinant acting through it. The draft adds that link.

paragraphs.text: Nedvetzki et al. (2003) showed that cells transfected with CD44vRA or with wildtype CD44v3-v10 bound FGF2 equally. However, cells immobilizing FGF2 through CD44vRA bound more soluble FGFR1 and stimulated proliferation of FGFR1-bearing cells more efficiently. Primary RA synovial fluid cells expressing CD44vRA also bound more soluble FGFR1. The authors suggested that the enhanced FGF2-FGFR1 interaction may foster the destructive inflammatory cascade in RA.

checks.claim: Cells transfected with CD44vRA or with wildtype CD44v3-v10 bound FGF2 equally.
checks.evidence_quote: CD44-negative Namalwa cells transfected with CD44vRA cDNA or with CD44v3-v10 (CD44vRA wild type) cDNA bound FGF-2 to an equal extent via their associated heparan sulfate chains.

checks.claim: Cells immobilizing FGF2 through CD44vRA bound more soluble FGFR1 than cells with wildtype CD44v3-v10.
checks.evidence_quote: Namalwa cells, immobilizing FGF-2 via their cell surface CD44vRA, bound substantially more soluble FGF receptor-1 (FGFR-1) than did Namalwa cells immobilizing the same amount of FGF-2 via their cell surface CD44v3-v10.

checks.claim: Cells immobilizing FGF2 through CD44vRA stimulated proliferation of FGFR1-bearing cells more efficiently.
checks.evidence_quote: The former cells stimulated the proliferation of BaF-32 cells, bearing FGFR-1, more efficiently than did the latter cells.

checks.claim: Primary RA synovial fluid cells expressing CD44vRA bound more soluble FGFR1.
checks.evidence_quote: isolated primary synovial fluid cells from RA patients expressing CD44vRA bound more soluble FGFR-1 to their cell surface-associated FGF-2 than did corresponding synovial cells expressing CD44v3-v10 or synovial cells from osteoarthritis patients

checks.claim: Nedvetzki et al. (2003) suggested that the enhanced FGF2-FGFR1 interaction via CD44vRA may foster the destructive inflammatory cascade in RA.
checks.evidence_quote: FGF-2 attached to the heparan sulfate moiety expressed by the novel CD44 variant of RA synovium cells exhibits an augmented ability to stimulate FGFR-1-mediated activities. A similar mechanism may foster the destructive inflammatory cascade not only in RA
checks.explanation: The authors propose that this mechanism may foster the inflammatory cascade in RA. They also mention other autoimmune diseases.

paragraphs.text: Suzuki et al. (2003) found that the RA-susceptibility PADI4 haplotype affected transcript stability and was associated with levels of antibody to citrullinated peptide in RA sera. PADI4 was expressed in hematologic tissues and RA synovial tissues. The authors suggested that the haplotype increases production of citrullinated autoantigens.

checks.claim: The RA-susceptibility PADI4 haplotype affected transcript stability.
checks.evidence_quote: a haplotype of PADI4 associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis that affected stability of transcripts

checks.claim: The RA-susceptibility PADI4 haplotype was associated with levels of antibody to citrullinated peptide in RA sera.
checks.evidence_quote: was associated with levels of antibody to citrullinated peptide in sera from individuals with rheumatoid arthritis

checks.claim: PADI4 was expressed in hematologic tissues and RA synovial tissues.
checks.evidence_quote: PADI4 was expressed in hematological and rheumatoid arthritis synovial tissues.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (2003) suggested that the RA-susceptibility PADI4 haplotype increases production of citrullinated autoantigens.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results imply that the PADI4 haplotype associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis increases production of citrullinated peptides acting as autoantigens
checks.explanation: The claim restates the authors' conclusion as given in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Hill et al. (2003) noted that RA is associated with MHC class II molecules containing the shared epitope and that citrulline-containing proteins are specific targets of the IgG antibody response in RA. They showed that conversion of arginine to citrulline at the peptide position that interacts with the shared epitope significantly increased peptide-MHC affinity and activated CD4+ T cells in HLA-DRB1*0401 transgenic mice. They concluded that their results revealed how shared epitope-carrying DRB1 alleles could initiate an autoimmune response to citrullinated self-antigens.

checks.claim: Hill et al. (2003) noted that RA is associated with MHC class II molecules containing the shared epitope.
checks.evidence_quote: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is genetically associated with MHC class II molecules that contain the shared epitope.

checks.claim: Hill et al. (2003) noted that citrulline-containing proteins are specific targets of the IgG antibody response in RA.
checks.evidence_quote: recent work has identified posttranslationally modified proteins containing citrulline (deiminated arginine) as specific targets of the IgG Ab response in RA patients

checks.claim: Conversion of arginine to citrulline at the peptide position that interacts with the shared epitope significantly increased peptide-MHC affinity.
checks.evidence_quote: the conversion of arginine to citrulline at the peptide side-chain position interacting with the shared epitope significantly increases peptide-MHC affinity

checks.claim: Conversion of arginine to citrulline at the shared-epitope-interacting peptide position activated CD4+ T cells in HLA-DRB1*0401 transgenic mice.
checks.evidence_quote: significantly increases peptide-MHC affinity and leads to the activation CD4(+) T cells in DR4-IE tg mice
checks.explanation: DR4-IE tg mice are the HLA-DRB1*0401 transgenic mice.

checks.claim: Hill et al. (2003) concluded that their results revealed how shared epitope-carrying DRB1 alleles could initiate an autoimmune response to citrullinated self-antigens.
checks.evidence_quote: These results reveal how DRB1 alleles with the shared epitope could initiate an autoimmune response to citrullinated self-Ags in RA patients.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion directly.

paragraphs.text: Lard et al. (2003) found that adenoviral transfer of IL10 to fibroblast-like synoviocytes inhibited their invasiveness. However, the invasiveness of these cells in vitro did not differ between -2849 G carriers and non-carriers.

checks.claim: Adenoviral transfer of IL10 to fibroblast-like synoviocytes inhibited their invasiveness.
checks.evidence_quote: Although adenoviral gene transfer of IL-10 to FLS inhibited their invasiveness

checks.claim: The in vitro invasiveness of fibroblast-like synoviocytes did not differ between IL10 -2849 G carriers and non-carriers.
checks.evidence_quote: no differences were observed in vitro in the FLS from RA patients who were -2849 non-G carriers compared with those who were G carriers.

paragraphs.text: Schönland et al. (2003) found that HLA-DRB1*04 alleles were associated with excessive telomere loss in CD4+ T cells of healthy individuals. The erosion occurred during the first 2 decades of life and was followed by reduced homeostatic T-cell proliferation in adulthood. Granulocytes were also affected, suggesting that the hematopoietic stem cell is the primary target. The authors proposed that HLA-DRB1*04 alleles, or genes in linkage disequilibrium with them, regulate stem cell replication and contribute to the accumulation of senescent and autoreactive T cells in RA.

checks.claim: HLA-DRB1*04 alleles were associated with excessive telomere loss in CD4+ T cells of healthy individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: In healthy individuals, HLA-DRB1*04 alleles were associated with excessive loss of telomeres in CD4+ T cells.

checks.claim: Telomere erosion in CD4+ T cells of HLA-DRB1*04 carriers occurred during the first 2 decades of life.
checks.evidence_quote: Accelerated telomeric erosion occurred during the first two decades of life

checks.claim: Telomere erosion in HLA-DRB1*04 carriers was followed by reduced homeostatic T-cell proliferation in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: Accelerated telomeric erosion occurred during the first two decades of life and was followed by reduced homeostatic T cell proliferation during adulthood.

checks.claim: Granulocytes of HLA-DRB1*04 carriers were also affected by telomere loss, suggesting that the hematopoietic stem cell is the primary target.
checks.evidence_quote: Premature telomeric loss also affected granulocytes, suggesting that the hematopoietic stem cell is the primary target.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly. In context, the premature loss refers to HLA-DRB1*04 carriers.

checks.claim: Schönland et al. (2003) proposed that HLA-DRB1*04 alleles, or genes in linkage disequilibrium with them, regulate stem cell replication and contribute to the accumulation of senescent and autoreactive T cells in RA.
checks.evidence_quote: We propose that HLA-DRB1*04 alleles or genes in linkage disequilibrium regulate stem cell replication and contribute to the accumulation of senescent and autoreactive T cells in rheumatoid arthritis.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this proposal directly.

paragraphs.text: Tokuhiro et al. (2003) showed that SLC22A4 expression is specific to hematologic and immunologic tissues. SLC22A4 was also highly expressed in the inflamed joints of mice with collagen-induced arthritis.

checks.claim: SLC22A4 expression is specific to hematologic and immunologic tissues.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that expression of SLC22A4 is specific to hematological and immunological tissues

checks.claim: SLC22A4 was highly expressed in the inflamed joints of mice with collagen-induced arthritis.
checks.evidence_quote: SLC22A4 is also highly expressed in the inflammatory joints of mice with collagen-induced arthritis.

paragraphs.text: Sakaguchi et al. (2003) reported that altered T-cell receptor signaling through an aberrant ZAP-70 changed the thresholds of thymic selection, so that autoimmune T cells were positively selected. They suggested that a genetically determined shift of the T-cell repertoire toward high self-reactivity might be crucial in a subset of RA patients. Ito et al. (2014) similarly proposed that genetic variation in T cell signaling molecules might alter thymic selection and thereby generate an autoimmune TCR repertoire.

checks.claim: Sakaguchi et al. (2003) reported that altered T-cell receptor signaling through an aberrant ZAP-70 changed the thresholds of thymic selection so that autoimmune T cells were positively selected.
checks.evidence_quote: Altered signal transduction from T-cell antigen receptor through the aberrant ZAP-70 changes the thresholds of T cells to thymic selection, leading to the positive selection of otherwise negatively selected autoimmune T cells.

checks.claim: Sakaguchi et al. (2003) suggested that a genetically determined shift of the T-cell repertoire toward high self-reactivity might be crucial in a subset of RA patients.
checks.evidence_quote: Thymic production of arthritogenic T cells due to a genetically determined selection shift of the T-cell repertoire towards high self-reactivity might also be crucial to the development of disease in a subset of patients with RA.

checks.claim: Ito et al. (2014) proposed that genetic variation in T cell signaling molecules might alter thymic selection and thereby generate an autoimmune TCR repertoire.
checks.evidence_quote: given that genetic polymorphism in a signaling molecule in T cells is a major determinant of genetic susceptibility to various human autoimmune diseases including RA, such a genetic variation might, at least in part, alter thymic selection, hence forming a TCR repertoire for causing autoimmune disease.

paragraphs.text: Because the same PTPN22 allele had been implicated in type 1 diabetes, Begovich et al. (2004) suggested that the variant phosphatase may increase overall immune reactivity.

checks.claim: The same PTPN22 allele associated with RA had been implicated in type 1 diabetes.
checks.evidence_quote: The minor allele of this SNP recently was implicated in type 1 diabetes

checks.claim: Begovich et al. (2004) suggested that the variant PTPN22 phosphatase may increase overall immune reactivity.

However, the draft says it was made because of the type 1 diabetes finding, while the paper draws it from the RA association together with the type 1 diabetes finding. The draft also leaves out the second half of the suggestion: a higher risk of autoimmune disease for carriers.

paragraphs.text: Lundberg et al. (2005) hypothesized that, in individuals with the appropriate genetic background, subclinical inflammation, possibly outside the joints (for example smoking-induced lung inflammation in carriers of the shared epitope), induces citrullination of endogenous proteins and anti-citrullinated protein antibodies that potentiate an inflammatory trigger in joints. They noted that an immune response to a citrullinated protein is not sufficient to induce arthritis and that genetic and environmental factors most probably both contribute.

checks.claim: Lundberg et al. (2005) hypothesized that, in genetically predisposed individuals, subclinical inflammation, possibly outside the joints, induces citrullination of endogenous proteins and anti-citrullinated protein antibodies that potentiate an inflammatory trigger in joints.

checks.claim: Lundberg et al. (2005) gave smoking-induced lung inflammation in carriers of the shared epitope as an example of extra-articular subclinical inflammation that could induce citrullination.
checks.explanation: the audit returned no verdict for this claim

checks.claim: Lundberg et al. (2005) noted that an immune response to a citrullinated protein is not sufficient to induce arthritis.
checks.explanation: the audit returned no verdict for this claim

checks.claim: Lundberg et al. (2005) noted that genetic and environmental factors most probably both contribute to RA.

paragraphs.text: Seyler et al. (2005) examined 72 rheumatoid synovial tissues. Synovitis containing ectopic germinal centers had the highest levels of APRIL, which was produced exclusively by CD83+ dendritic cells.
